newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot electricity extends gain on natgas rise.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot electricity extends gain on natgas rise.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the Electricity Reliability Council of Texas (EROT) extended Tuesday's gain on the continued rise in natural gas market, market sources said.

Despite resumption of normal natgas supply from the U.S. Gulf after the passage of Tropical Storm Josephine, cash natgas values surged today amid bullish outlook for spot demand and storage injection, power traders said.
Swing natgas for power generation within ERCOT was pegged at $2.30-$2.35 per million British thermal units, up five to 10 cents from Tuesday.

Lower Colorado River Authority's 430 megawatt (MW) Ferguson gas station in Marble Falls, Tx., was scheduled to return to service some time today after being shut last Thursday following a superheater tube rupture.
Peak, firm electricity in ERCOT for Thursday was quoted at $22.50-$23.75 a megawatt hour (MWh), and was talked as high as $26.50, up from Tuesday's $21.00-$23.00 range for Wednesday delivery.
Off-peak, firm ERCOT power for Thursday was discussed near $12.00, compared with a quote $12.00-$14.00 on Tuesday.
November ERCOT electricity was pegged near $20.25 a MWh, versus Tuesday's range at $19.50-$20.50.
December ERCOT power was valued near $22.00.
